summary: Tested Credit Card Bill Payment tier boundary change (NEW: ₹0-₹50,000 → ₹15 ; ₹50,001-₹1,00,000 → ₹25 ; >₹1,00,000 BLOCKED). 13/13 backend pytest cases PASS and full frontend Playwright suite PASS. Backend service_charge correct at boundaries 1, 24999, 25000, 25001, 49999, 50000 (=₹15) and 50001, 75000, 99999, 100000 (=₹25). Hard cap (100001) returns HTTP 400 'Bill amount cannot exceed ₹1,00,000' and does NOT debit wallet. End-to-end ₹50,000→₹50,015 then ₹50,001→₹50,026 verified with exact wallet debits. Historical transactions remain frozen (no retro recalc). Frontend right-side SERVICE CHARGES panel shows exactly two rows '₹0 – ₹50,000 → ₹15' and '₹50,001 – ₹1,00,000 → ₹25' in dark green (#1B4332). Live Pay button totals correct at all 5 boundary inputs (10K, 50K, 50001, 75K, 1L). Over-limit shows inline rose error + disabled 'Amount exceeds limit' button. Old ₹25,000 boundary not present anywhere in UI.
critical_code_review_comments: Single source of truth (calcServiceCharge in /app/frontend/src/lib/billing.js + inline backend literal at server.py:769) — boundary value 50000 is duplicated across backend and frontend; consider moving the threshold to backend-served config in future to make this truly one source.
RechargeIn schema requires screenshot_path but it is a free-form string with no upload-validation enforcement at this endpoint — minor pre-existing concern, unrelated to this change.

BillPay.jsx Pay button shows total with two decimals (e.g. 'Pay ₹50,015.00 from Wallet'); review request examples wrote 'Pay ₹50,015' without decimals. Substring match still PASS but cosmetic — main agent may decide whether to drop trailing .00 for integer totals.
